title: Manager prep - Q1 2026
content:
Manager prep notes for 1:1 / skip-level / performance calibration. Quick, messy - for discussion with Lena.

Context / role focus:
- I lead onboarding improvements, early-career development program, and hiring process efficiency projects.
- Priority this quarter: lower time-to-productivity for new hires, stabilize onboarding docs, scale buddy program.

Top accomplishments (since last review):
- Launched v2 onboarding curriculum (pilot): consolidated 12 docs into 4 modules, introduced first-week checkpoints. Pilot cohort (6 new hires) reported 25% higher confidence in core workflows in week 2 (survey N=6).
- Reduced average new-hire ADP (active days to product) from ~28 days -> ~24 days for engineering hires where we owned onboarding flows (measured across 10 hires, rolling 3 months).
- Built automated onboarding checklist in Notion + Slack reminders (integration with HR system). Cut manual follow-ups by ~40% (measured by time spent by ops team).
- Rolled out buddy pairing program for ICs <1yr; paired 18 people, 85% reported the pairing was helpful (quick pulse).
- Helped unblock 3 hiring reqs by pairing with recruiting ops and reducing process steps - saved ~2 weeks per req on average.

Metrics to call out / evidence:
- New hire survey scores: onboarding NPS from pilot = +18 (baseline pilot vs previous cohort). Raw responses attached in Confluence page PO-ONBOARD-2026.
- Time saved for ops: internal time-tracking shows ~6 hours/week reallocated after automation (across 3 people).
- Hiring pipeline velocity: 2 reqs sped up by ~14 days from completion to offer.

What worked well:
- Cross-functional syncs with Eng Managers and Recruiting: weekly 30-min cadence was high ROI.
- Running a small pilot first - got qualitative feedback quickly and iterated docs.
- Using Slack check-ins to surface blockers early.

Areas to improve / open questions:
- Scaling beyond pilot: documentation ownership unclear for some modules (who keeps them updated?). Need to assign doc owners and set a quarterly review cadence.
- Onboarding for PMs and Design: more bespoke needs; current curriculum too eng-focused. Proposal: light-track + role-specific add-ons.
- Measurement: need a standardized definition of "time to productivity" for cross-team comparisons. Current metric is noisy.
- Feedback loop: pair onboarding pulses with manager check-ins to capture skill ramp (not just confidence).

Requests for manager (Lena):
- Help make doc ownership ask to leadership (product/design managers) - a short email or mention in next leadership sync would help.
- Support for two headcount asks: one rotational onboarding coordinator (6mo contract) and one part-time analytics help to clean the metric definitions and dashboards.
- Advice on performance calibration approach: I think my impact is solid but not fully visible in OKR metrics. Should I prepare a short 2-slide summary for calibration with concrete numbers and pilot testimonials?

Career / development notes (for conversation):
- Goal: move toward manager-of-managers scope in 12-18 months - want to get experience with cross-team programs and some direct management (2-3 ICs).
- What I need: exposure to strategic roadmap conversations and mentorship on scaling programs. Would value 1-2 shadowing sessions with you for leadership rituals (staff+ manager planning).

Potential talking points for 1:1:
- Quick wins: highlight the onboarding pilot results + metric improvements (be specific: 24 days ADP, NPS +18).
- Long-term: roadmap to roll out role-specific tracks for PM/design + owner model for docs.
- Headcount ask: justify coordinator (expected ROI: free up 6-8 hours/week from senior ops and reduce manual triage; payback within 3 months if we scale hiring).
- Calibration: request prep guidance and share proposed 2-slide summary template.

Risks / blockers to flag:
- If we don't assign doc owners, docs will drift and pilot gains will decay.
- Resource constraint for analytics means we have noisy signals; may slow executive buy-in.
- Hiring freezes / shifting priorities could delay rollout - contingency: lightweight playbooks that don't require full staffing.

To do (next 2 weeks):
- Draft short owner-request email to product/design leads (put in drive; want Lena sign-off).
- Finalize pilot survey summary / screenshots in Confluence.
- Put a prioritization list of onboarding modules (top 4) and recommended owners.
- Draft the 2-slide calibration summary (numbers + 3 quotes from pilot).

Notes to self (quick informal):
- When presenting metrics, focus on absolute change (days saved) + qualitative quotes - execs respond to both.
- Keep ask small and concrete: 0.5 FTE analytics or 6-month coordinator.
- Follow up with recruiting on the 3 reqs we sped up - capture process changes so they can be reused.

Links / references:
- Confluence: PO-ONBOARD-2026 (pilot writeup + raw survey).
- Jira: HR-462 (automation of reminders).
- Slack: #people-ops-onboarding (pilot feedback thread).

End of notes.

(Will clean this up into a short doc for skip-level if Lena thinks it's worth sharing)
